templates.name: Excavation — Daily Competent Person Inspection
templates.notes: Also run per_event after rainstorms or other hazard-increasing occurrences. Reconcile item list against Fed OSHA 1926 Subpart P or Cal/OSHA as applicable, and company HASP.

items.text: Inspection performed prior to start of work and as needed throughout shift
Soil classification confirmed/re-confirmed for current conditions (record type)
Excavation depth at deepest point (record)
Protective system (slope/bench/shield/shoring) appropriate for soil type and depth, and in sound condition
Shield/shoring used within tabulated data or manufacturer limits; certification available on site
Safe access/egress (ladder/ramp) within required travel distance of all workers
Spoils, materials, and equipment set back from excavation edge per required distance
No water accumulation, or water controls (dewatering) functioning with dedicated monitoring
No signs of tension cracks, sloughing, fissures, or surcharge distress
Adjacent structures, roadways, and utilities protected/supported; no undermining observed
Underground utilities located, marked, and protected; USA/811 ticket current (record ticket no.)
Atmospheric testing performed where hazardous atmosphere could reasonably exist (record readings)
Barricades, covers, and public protection in place
Weather since last inspection considered (rain, freeze/thaw); re-inspection triggers noted
Photo of excavation and protective system condition

templates.name: Dewatering — Discharge Monitoring Log
templates.notes: Reconcile fields and frequencies against the actual discharge permit / WDR / municipal authorization. Permit conditions govern; add value items for any numeric limits it imposes.

items.text: Discharge location matches permitted point of discharge
Treatment/BMPs in place and functioning (weir tank, filter bag, sediment trap as specified)
Visual check: discharge clear, no sheen, no odor, no visible sediment plume
Estimated discharge flow rate (record)
Turbidity reading, if required by permit (record)
pH reading, if required by permit (record)
No erosion or scour at point of discharge; energy dissipation in place
Totalized/estimated volume this period (record)
Photo of discharge point and BMPs

templates.name: Water Main Disinfection — Chlorination / Flushing / Bac-T (AWWA C651)
templates.notes: Subject is the main segment (station-to-station). All numeric acceptance values (initial dose, residual at end of contact period, contact duration, flushing velocity, sample count/spacing) are governed by the AWWA C651 edition referenced in the spec and any project-specific overrides — confirm before first use. Dechlorination of flushing water is typically required before discharge; coordinate with the dewatering/discharge log.

items.text: Segment identification: main size, material, limits (station-to-station) recorded
Pre-chlorination flush completed to remove debris (record method/duration)
Chlorination method used (continuous feed / slug / tablet) per spec
Initial chlorine residual at far end after fill (record)
Contact period start date/time recorded
Chlorine residual at end of contact period (record)
Contact period duration met per spec (record)
Valves operated during chlorination to disinfect appurtenances (as required)
Final flush completed; heavily chlorinated water dechlorinated and disposed per permit
Post-flush chlorine residual comparable to distribution system (record)
Bacteriological samples collected — count, locations, and collector per district requirements (record)
Lab results received: all samples passing (attach lab report)
District/owner acceptance to place in service received (record name/date)
